eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study uses non‑linear AI models on adult lung transplant recipients, but it does not compare the predictions to current clinical practice (gold standard), lacking a required comparator.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: National Research Association (ANR) (Inflamex renewal 10-LABX-0017), Consejería de Universidades, fondos FEDER de la Junta de Andalucía (ProyExec_0499), DHU FIRE Emergence 4, l’Agence de la Biomedecine
identification_methods.Setting: Hospital-based clinical cohort of lung transplant patients
identification_methods.Comments: Open access article; uses recycled dataset from a previous study on soluble CD31 risk prediction
identification_methods.Institution: Université Sorbonne Paris Nord, LAGA, CNRS, UMR 7539, Laboratoire d’excellence Inflamex, Villetaneuse, France
identification_methods.Address: University of Malaga, Department of Genetics, MLiMO, 29010, Málaga, Spain
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Personalised Risk Predictor for Acute Cellular Rejection in Lung Transplant Using Soluble CD31 (previous study)
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included 40 lung transplant patients; 7 (17.5%) experienced acute cellular rejection within one year
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Multilayer Perceptron, Autoencoder, Random Forest, k-Nearest Neighbours, Gaussian Naive Bayes
identification_methods.Class Imbalance: Handled by stratified k‑fold cross‑validation and balanced mini‑batches (≈5% of each class per batch)
identification_methods.Comparator: Standard machine learning models without topological improvement
identification_methods.Input Variables: CD31 H24, CD31 H48, CD31 H72, PaO2/FiO2 H24, PaO2/FiO2 H48, PaO2/FiO2 H72, SOFA respiratory H24, SOFA respiratory H48, SOFA respiratory H72
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Proposed topological autoencoder (Taelcore) with topological loss based on persistence diagram entropy; class balancing in mini‑batches; evaluation using KL divergence, RMSE, TRUST, MSE

population.Population Notes: Clinical dataset of 40 patients; 7 (17.5%) experienced acute cellular rejection within one year.
population.Diagnosis: Emphysema (33%), interstitial lung disease (50%), other etiologies (17.5%)
population.Diagnosis Overall: Emphysema (33%), interstitial lung disease (50%), other etiologies (17.5%)

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: Taelcore (topological autoencoder with best linear combination), also using Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Autoencoder (AE)
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Clinical numeric variables (CD31 levels, PaO2/FiO2 ratios, SOFA respiratory scores) measured during first 3 days post‑transplant
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline data (measurements within first 3 days)
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Topological autoencoder (Taelcore) combines TDA (Rips filtration, persistence diagrams, entropy vectorisation) with machine learning classifiers; grid search for hyper‑parameters; stratified k‑fold cross‑validation; 75/25 train‑test split
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Prediction of acute cellular rejection (ACR) risk after lung transplantation
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome is binary classification of ACR vs non‑ACR within one year
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Applying topological improvement increased MLP accuracy from 80% to 90%; overall model achieved 90% accuracy for ACR prediction
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Classification accuracy on held‑out test set after applying Taelcore dimensionality reduction
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Significant improvement over baseline model without topological features
